title: OPA policy-based routing for on-prem telemetry collectors to guarantee tenant isolation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: On-prem and VPC collectors currently rely on rule-based routing in the collector binary and edge proxies. This approach has resulted in opaque routing decisions, increased blast radius when misconfigurations occur, and makes auditability for regulated private customers difficult. Goal: Introduce a pluggable policy evaluation layer (OPA) into the on-prem collector path that enforces tenant-scoped routing decisions, emits rich audit traces/events, and provides a single source of truth for routing rules between Dedicated and Private deployments. Scope: - Integrate Open Policy Agent (server-side library mode) into the collector process so policy checks execute before telemetry is forwarded to tenant pipelines. - Define a canonical policy schema that accepts envelope metadata (tenant_id, origin_cluster, cert_fingerprint, route_hint) and returns routing actions (allow/deny, target_pipeline, audit_labels, sample_rate). - Add structured audit events and trace spans for every policy decision (policy_id, input_hash, decision, reason, matched_rule). - Expose a read-only policy management API for private install admins to preview and dry-run policies locally. - Ensure fallback safe-mode: mis-evaluations or OPA failures must default to deny-by-default and generate PagerDuty alerts for enterprise customers. Out of scope: policy authoring UI (this ticket is infra and runtime only). Success metrics: - Zero cross-tenant routing violations in a 90-day post-deploy window. - Policy decision latency <= 1ms p50 added to end-to-end ingest path for typical collector CPU profiles. - Audit event storage cost increase < 7% for typical deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Collector binary includes OPA-based evaluation step and loads policies from configured directory or management endpoint
Policy schema documented in Confluence and validated with unit tests
Every routing decision emits a structured audit event and an associated trace span with policy metadata
Fail-closed behavior verified in integration tests and simulated network failure scenarios
Benchmark shows policy evaluation adds <= 1ms p50 latency on our standard on-prem collector image
Deployment runbook and rollback steps added to runbooks/obs/tickets and reviewed by SRE
implementation_notes: We will use OPA as an embedded library (rego compiled to WASM is an option, but initial implementation should embed OPA to avoid adding wasm runtime complexity). Policy filesystem sync path will be /etc/redwood/policies and a management endpoint (optional) will be reachable over mTLS for centrally managed private installs. Evaluation happens after envelope parsing but before KV cache/prefix lookups to avoid unnecessary work for denied traces. For performance, compile frequently used policies and cache compiled evaluators per-worker thread. Provide a sidecar compatibility shim for older private installations that cannot upgrade their collector immediately: a lightweight policy-proxy binary that exposes the same local API and forwards to external OPA. Audit events should be written as structured logs with a consistent schema: {timestamp, tenant_id, decision, policy_id, matched_rule, origin, request_id, cert_fingerprint}.
tradeoffs: Embedding OPA increases collector binary size and adds a small CPU cost; alternate approach (external OPA service) reduces binary size but increases network fragility and latency variability
Using WASM-compiled policies would reduce collector memory churn but adds complexity in managing wasm runtime versions
Strict deny-by-default improves safety for regulated customers but may increase false-positive drops during rollout; mitigations include dry-run mode and per-tenant policy exceptions
test_plan: Unit tests for policy schema validation and rule matching
Microbenchmarks across our supported CPU families (x86-cloud, arm64-edge) to measure p50/p95 added latency
Integration tests simulating policy misconfigurations and network partitions to verify fail-closed behavior
E2E test with a private cluster (staging-onprem) with synthetic multi-tenant traffic and audit log export verified to S3-compatible store
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy to internal staging-onprem with dry-run mode enabled for 2 weeks
Beta: enable enforcement for non-critical tenants and run enforcement for 1 week with elevated monitoring
GA: enable enforcement for all tenants alongside runbook, with PagerDuty escalation for any policy-engine failures
risks: Policy misconfiguration could cause tenant telemetry loss if not caught during dry-run
Embedded OPA could increase memory usage on very small on-prem appliances (mitigation: resource limits and sidecar option)
Policy management complexity for customers who want fine-grained rules across many pipelines (mitigation: provide example policy library and validation tooling)
